title: VPN for Windows & Mac: Setup Guide for PC and Laptop
description: Using a VPN on Windows, Mac and Linux: apps vs built-in settings, kill switches, browser extensions, sharing a VPN with a console and common fixes.
cardText: Apps vs built-in settings, browser extensions, kill switches and fixing connection problems.
h1: VPNs for Windows, Mac and Linux
intro: On a computer you can use your provider’s app, the system’s built-in VPN settings or a browser extension. Here’s the difference, and how to make sure everything is really protected.

image.alt: MacBook Pro on a desk showing lines of code

sections.h2: App, built-in settings or browser extension?
sections.html:
• Provider app (recommended): the easiest way to get a kill switch, leak protection, split tunnelling and automatic updates.
  • Built-in VPN settings: Windows and macOS can connect to some VPN types (such as IKEv2) without an app, using details from your provider. Useful for work VPNs, but you may lose app-only features.
  • Browser extension: usually protects only that browser’s traffic, not your other apps. Some providers’ extensions act as a proxy rather than a full VPN.

• Kill switch (sometimes called “network lock”).
  • Launch and connect on start-up.
  • DNS leak protection, and IPv6 leak protection if your connection uses IPv6.
  • Split tunnelling for apps that don’t work well over the VPN, such as some banking or work tools.

Then run a leak test to check.

• Won’t connect: try another server or protocol, check your firewall or antivirus, and update the app.
  • Slow speeds: try a closer server and WireGuard; compare with a speed test without the VPN.
  • Sites blocking you: some sites block VPN IP addresses; try another server or split tunnelling.
  • Work laptop: follow your employer’s IT policy. Installing another VPN may conflict with the company VPN.

faqs.q: Do Windows and Mac have a built-in VPN?
faqs.a: They have built-in VPN clients that can connect to a VPN server, but not a VPN service. You still need a provider (or your employer’s VPN) to connect to.

faqs.q: Is a VPN browser extension enough?
faqs.a: Usually not for full protection: most extensions only cover that browser. Use the full app if you want every app on your computer protected.

faqs.q: Can I share my laptop’s VPN with a games console?
faqs.a: Yes. Windows and macOS can share an internet connection over Ethernet or Wi‑Fi, so a console can use the laptop’s VPN connection. A VPN router is a simpler long-term option.
